title: Mitochondrial fission factor senses and governs ferroptosis.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: paper_context.py: no PMCID, Europe PMC flags all N (not open access, no supplement, no text-mined accessions, no NCBI links to GEO/SRA/BioProject, no Zenodo/Dryad hit). PRIDE (proteomics repository) keyword searches for 'MFF ferroptosis', 'ferroptosis phosphoproteomics', 'ferroptosis' (50 most recent) and 'mitochondrial fission factor' returned no project matching this paper. One web search found only the paywalled Nature page and news write-ups, no repository accession.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Abstract and news coverage only: quantitative phosphoproteomics comparing cells treated with ferroptosis inducers (RSL3, erastin) versus apoptosis (staurosporine) and necroptosis inducers; MFF Ser155 phosphorylation, MFF-SPARK biosensor, PKCβ/DUSP22, avermectin B1. No sample counts, site counts or data availability statement were seen.

a1_downloadable.note: No open full text, no supplement, and no PRIDE/GEO/Zenodo/Dryad deposit found by DOI or keyword; the phosphoproteomics may sit in iProX (Chinese proteomics repository) but no accession was visible because the paper is paywalled.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Not checked in files. A 'ferroptosis-selective phosphosite' label would have to be constructed by differential analysis across a handful of treatment conditions, not a measured column.

a5_enough_rows.note: Unknown. The design is a few cell-death treatments with replicates, so the number of independent samples is likely tens, not thousands; row count not seen.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: unknown; processed phosphosite tables would be small
a6_fits_laptop.note: Not checked; processed proteomics tables are typically under 100 MB.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: No counts available from either paper or files.

a8_label_provenance.note: Any label would be derived from the same phosphoproteomics intensities used as features (fold change thresholds), risking circularity.

backbone.name: ESM-2, a protein language model (would apply only to phosphosite sequence windows)

integration.partner_dataset: PhosphoSitePlus / FerrDb (ferroptosis regulator database), in principle
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Not writable without the phosphosite table; no data located.

controls.positive_control: MFF Ser155 should rank as a ferroptosis-specific phosphosite (paper's own finding).

honest_claim_h3: At best: ranks phosphosites by ferroptosis-specificity in one or a few cell lines under four death-inducing treatments, which is a differential-analysis result, not an ML prediction.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use protein phosphorylation changes after different cell-death drugs to predict which phosphorylation sites are specific to iron-driven cell death.
plain_idea.train_on: Phosphorylation site intensities from cells treated with ferroptosis, apoptosis or necroptosis inducers; number of samples and sites unknown because no data file was found.
plain_idea.predict: Whether a site is ferroptosis-selective, which would itself come from fold-change comparisons in the same measurements.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Ferroptosis researchers could prioritise regulators, but this mostly duplicates the paper's own differential analysis, so the ML value is low.

ml_idea: Classify phosphosites as ferroptosis-selective from sequence context and abundance profiles; abandoned because no data were found and the label is constructed from the same intensities.

effort.cheapest_killing_check: Find the phosphoproteomics accession in the paper's data availability statement (likely iProX/PRIDE) and count samples; already fails on missing data.

verdict_reason: Paywalled mechanistic cell-biology paper with no located data deposit (A1 fails): no PMCID, no supplement, no PRIDE/GEO/Zenodo match. Even if the phosphoproteome is found, it covers a few treatment conditions, and any label would be constructed from the same intensities (A2/A8).
